counterpart_properties.description: Optical phase-space acceptance of a collection channel, set by its effective aperture area and accepted solid-angle range for incoming radiation.
counterpart_properties.documentation:
Étendue is the optical phase-space acceptance of a collection channel, describing the area–solid-angle product admitted for radiation transport. It characterizes optical throughput rather than emitted radiance or detector efficiency.

For a uniform acceptance, the étendue $G$ is defined by

$$
G = A\Omega
$$

where $A$ is the effective aperture area and $\Omega$ is the accepted solid angle. More generally, the same quantity is the integral of differential area–solid-angle acceptance over the admitted optical phase space.

The geometric quantity may be specialized by weighting the admitted phase space with a wavelength response, as in [spectral étendue of a spectrometer channel](name:spectral_etendue_of_spectrometer_channel). It remains distinct from [spectrometer-channel efficiency](name:efficiency_of_spectrometer_channel), which describes transmission to the active detector after optical-path losses.

Positioning (19/20): The documentation clearly positions itself above the child, using a proper name: link, and also distinguishes itself from the sibling etendue_of_spectrometer for additional context; minor dock because two cross-references are packed into one sentence which could slightly blur which is the direct child vs a sibling. Physics accuracy (20/20): The étendue definition, non-negativity, and the explicit exclusion of radiance/power/signal/spectral-intensity interpretations are all physically correct at the generalized level; no child-level specifics are needed or missing. counterpart_properties.description: Optical phase-space acceptance of a radiation-collection channel, determined by its aperture extent and accepted solid-angle range.
counterpart_properties.documentation:
Etendue is the optical phase-space acceptance of a radiation-collection channel. It quantifies how much radiance can be transferred through the channel's collecting aperture and accepted ray directions.

For a general optical system, etendue is defined by

$$
G = \int_A \int_{\Omega} \cos\theta\,d\Omega\,dA
$$

where $G$ is the etendue, $A$ is the collecting-aperture area, $\Omega$ is the accepted solid-angle region, $dA$ and $d\Omega$ are differential area and solid angle, and $\theta$ is the angle between an accepted ray and the local aperture normal. For uniform acceptance near normal incidence, this reduces to $G \approx A\Omega$. Spectral variants, such as [spectral etendue of a spectrometer channel](name:spectral_etendue_of_spectrometer_channel), may apply wavelength-response weighting while retaining the same optical phase-space meaning. Etendue is non-negative and excludes detector conversion efficiency and radiometric calibration factors.

properties.documentation:
Optical étendue is the geometric phase-space acceptance of a radiation-collection system. It describes how the collecting area and range of accepted ray directions jointly determine the system's throughput for radiation from an observed source.

For an effective area and accepted solid angle, the étendue $G$ is defined by:

$$
G = A_{\mathrm{eff}}\Omega_{\mathrm{eff}}
$$

where $G$ is the optical étendue, $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective collecting area, and $\Omega_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the accepted solid angle.

The quantity applies to radiation entering an optical collection system from a plasma or other observed source and aggregates acceptance over the collecting area and accepted ray directions. It is non-negative and does not itself represent radiance, collected power, detector signal, or spectral intensity. The [spectral étendue of a spectrometer channel](name:spectral_etendue_of_spectrometer_channel) is a narrower response-weighted form in which the optical acceptance is weighted by the channel's wavelength response, while [étendue of a spectrometer](name:etendue_of_spectrometer) represents the corresponding unweighted spectrometer-level acceptance.
